topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines its core learning objectives regarding cancer therapies.

topics.label: Conventional cancer treatments and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss traditional local and systemic interventions, focusing on surgery, radiotherapy, cytotoxic chemotherapy, and non-specific drug resistance mechanisms.

topics.label: Exploiting cellular vulnerabilities and genetic defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine therapeutic strategies that exploit intrinsic tumor vulnerabilities, such as hormone receptor dependency, cell cycle checkpoint loss, and synthetic lethality.

topics.label: Targeting oncogenic kinases and kinase inhibitor resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on designing small-molecule inhibitors against oncogenic driver kinases and managing the subsequent development of drug resistance and bypass signaling.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the design and mechanisms of engineered monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates directed at cancer cell surface antigens.

topics.label: Harnessing immune responses and cancer immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the biological basis of tumor immune surveillance and immunotherapeutic modalities that reactivate or engineer T cells against cancer.

topics.label: Broader challenges, historical progress, and future directions in cancer management
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate overall trends in cancer mortality, persistent clinical challenges, and emerging paradigms in diagnosis, prevention, and treatment strategies.
